payload.body: Single-horned jiao dragons circle highland lakes where cloud shadows cool threshing floors daily. Solitary brow horns split mists quietly at dusk, leading lost boats toward lantern posts. After lake wardens rang bronze bells before storms hourly loudly, their circling paths steadied near guarded shores. Wardens tend bell ropes through mists nightly now steadily, guiding coils away from nets. Ordinary lakeside children return shed golden scales to waters dutifully after finding them ashore. In battle they descend between raiders and villagers swiftly, shielding with coiled bulk alone. Belled shores and lowered poles calm coils quickly during meetings in occupied shallows always. Hailstorms ground juveniles on high pastures yearly, where herders shelter them behind stone walls. This benevolent single-horned lake dragon shields boats with coiled bulk without casting spells. Its celebrated wingless glides and sudden stoops reflect trained muscle and weather sense rather than conjured sorcery. Seasonal movements follow water, pasture, and nesting cliffs that patient observers map without disturbing lairs. Shed feathers, scales, or molted quills circulate as keepsakes while living specimens remain wary and untouched. Mottled juveniles shelter within deep cover where solicitous parents deliver food throughout vulnerable early months. Careful wayfarers avoid provoking displays with lowered weapons, covered stores, and quiet detours around nests.
payload.base_appearance: Radiant gold serpentine dragon coils cloud-long impressively, single brow horn gleaming brightly. Scales gilded and rain-beaded, descent gentle before shields, flight wingless inside coiling mist. Its celebrated hybrid frame balances recognizable animal bulk with distinctive crests built for display and sudden assaults. Every scar, notch, and stain records ordinary weather, prey struggles, and narrow escapes from predators.
payload.portrait_brief: Its striking storied head fills the frame with crested brows, bright predatory eyes, and weather-worn hide around the muzzle. Harsh daylight exposes every nick, stain, and healed wound without flattery or ornament.
